title: Memory and learning are the origin of developmental modularity

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Memory and learning are the origin of developmental modularity

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Memory can be the beginning of modularity because learning compresses complex states into simple triggers; in somatic control networks this appears as developmental modules in which a single simple driver (e.g. a bioelectric state) initiates a complex morphogenetic cascade such as building an eye or hand.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2019, The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition › The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Importantly, memory can serve as the beginning of modularity because learning essentially groups diverse stimuli into compressed representations: complex states of affairs become remembered as compact biophysical engrams – this is the essence of the kind of modularity when a simple biophysical event kicks off the formation of a complex morphogenetic cascade such as building a “hand” in embryogenesis.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Computational Boundary of a "Self": Developmental Bioelectricity Drives Multicellularity and Scale-Free Cognition”, Frontiers in psychology (2019), doi:10.3389/fpsyg.2019.02688; section “The Agent’s Evolutionary Back-Story: Scaling of Information by Bioelectricity”. Scope: Developmental control networks in animals

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2019-boundary-13: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.30

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Existing developmental datasets can identify compact triggers and downstream modules. They generally cannot distinguish learned memory compression from evolved regulatory switching, so only a proxy for the mechanism is currently testable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Identify developmental systems where a compact, persistent physiological state triggers a complex morphological program, then test whether the state was acquired by learning-like history and functions as a compressed representation rather than an ordinary regulatory switch.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
A simple trigger is equally predicted by conventional gene-regulatory control.

Memory, learning, compression, and modularity have competing mappings.

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Bioelectric or genetic triggers of eyes and hands are real experimental facts. The claim says those modules originate as memory compressing complex states into simple engrams. A hierarchical gene network without memory produces the same trigger-to-anatomy map. No observation available today separates the memory origin from that non-cognitive description.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: A single trigger that starts eye or limb formation is a measurable developmental module. Identifying that module as memory, because learning compresses states into triggers, does not change the embryological outcome relative to an ordinary gene-regulatory hierarchy.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
No dataset records the evolutionary origin of modularity as learning.

Master-regulator cascades and memory engrams predict the same inductions.
